newsitem.title: USA: New York mayor's wife says she out of his politics.
newsitem.headline: New York mayor's wife says she out of his politics.

text.p: The wife of Mayor Rudolph Giuliani, facing allegations he is having an affair with an aide, says she has distanced herself from her husband's political life to focus on her journalism career.

"I wanted to remove myself from being a conduit to the mayor," Donna Hanover was quoted as saying in Liz Smith's syndicated gossip column on Wednesday. "I decided it would be better for me to choose my own focus, which is not political."

Hanover, a television anchor who has been married to Giuliani for 13 years, has said she would not be campaigning with him in this November's mayoral election. The Republican mayor is heavily favoured to win re-election.

Hanover appears on Fox television's "Good Day New York" and the Food Network. She also is a part-time actress and had a small role in the movie "The People vs. Larry Flynt." She no longer uses Giuliani's last name, and the couple rarely appears together in public.
The article in September's Vanity Fair said Giuliani has been having an affair with 32-year-old aide Cristyne Lategano.
Giuliani angrily denied the allegation, calling the article "untrue" and "malicious."

Asked about the crush of media coverage since the magazine released the article, Hanover told Smith, "I am a journalist myself, so I understand that reporters want to get both sides of every story. I didn't resent the press pursuing me."
The questions posed by the gossip columnist did not directly address Giuliani's reported infidelity, and Hanover did not mention it.
Hanover said she still considered herself the city's first lady, saying, "I like it and work hard at it."
The Vanity Fair article, which quoted unidentified sources and unidentified former aides, predicted Giuliani, 53, and Hanover, 46, would separate after the November election.
The couple has two children, Andrew, 11, and Caroline, 7.
